title: The Blind Specialist

sourceEvidence.locator: 1.1 The Bargain That Built the Modern World
sourceEvidence.excerpt: The first mistake in any critique of specialization is to romanticize the alternative. Before modern expertise, human beings did not walk around as integrated sages with balanced knowledge of ecology, medicine, politics, engineering, psychology, and the meaning of life. They mostly knew less, died earlier, and were confidently wrong about a larger number of things.

sourceEvidence.locator: 1.1 The Bargain That Built the Modern World
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Specialization is one of civilization's great compression techniques. It allows a person to inherit a long chain of accumulated knowledge without personally rediscovering it. A surgeon enters an operating room carrying centuries of anatomy, instruments, trials, failures, sterilization practices, imaging techniques, and tacit skill. A semiconductor engineer works inside a technical lineage so deep that no single participant could reconstruct the entire manufacturing stack from first principles. A security researcher can spend years on one class of protocol because the rest of the system is held, temporarily, by other minds.

sourceEvidence.locator: 1.1 The Bargain That Built the Modern World
sourceEvidence.excerpt: This is the first principle of the book: useful perception is selective. A map that contains every blade of grass is not a map. A model that preserves every detail is the thing itself. An expert field becomes powerful by deciding which distinctions matter and which can be ignored for a class of problems.

sourceEvidence.locator: 1.1 The Bargain That Built the Modern World
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Expertise has a psychological side effect. Repeatedly seeing things that non-specialists cannot see is intoxicating. The radiologist notices the shadow. The cryptographer spots the flawed assumption. The economist recognizes the incentive. The machine-learning researcher sees distribution shift. The historian hears an old pattern hiding inside new rhetoric. This is real competence. But the experience can quietly teach a second, false lesson: if my lens reveals hidden reality here, perhaps my lens reveals the hidden structure of reality in general.

hook: An expert sees the flaw everyone else missed, then overlooks the world outside that expertise.
readerPromise: Recognize how expertise's necessary selectivity can become unjustified authority outside its scope.
